title: Request Lifecycle and Controls Catalog — 2026
author: Priya N. Rao
body:
Purpose
-------
This catalog defines the lifecycle for operational requests and the associated control gates across Access & Permissions, Change Management, Data Management, Procurement & Expenses, Vendor Management, and Travel. It provides standardized request forms, approval matrices, SLAs, and template artifacts to reduce tribal knowledge and speed consistent decisions.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendor agents who submit or approve requests for: system access, configuration changes, data uses, purchases, vendor engagements, and company travel. Exceptions must be approved by the owning function and recorded in the exception registry.

Principles
----------
- Least privilege and just-in-time access.
- Separation of duties for financial and security-critical approvals.
- Automated enforcement where possible; manual review when risk exceeds automation thresholds.
- Clear SLAs and escalation paths for business continuity.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Requester: initiates the request with required justification and attachments.
- Approver: designated role(s) who evaluate and approve/reject per the approval matrix.
- Owner/Maintainer: team that implements the request (SRE, infra, facilities, travel ops).
- Security Reviewer: performs data/privacy/security review when flagged.
- Finance Reviewer: approves expenditures above configured thresholds.
- Legal Reviewer: reviews contracts, vendor terms, and high-risk data-sharing agreements.
- Compliance & Audit: retains records and performs periodic reviews.

Access & Permissions (IAM)
-------------------------
Purpose: Standardize requests for cloud/console/API access and role grants.

Access request flow (standard)
1. Requester completes Access Request form in ProcureFlow/IAM Portal including justification, duration, resource scope, and owner.
2. Auto-validation run by IAM Service: checks policy templates and existing memberships.
3. If low-risk (pre-approved role & <30 days) automatic grant occurs; otherwise routed to Approver(s).
4. Security Reviewer is added if role includes sensitive scopes (PII, audit logs, production write).
5. Owner executes grant and documents ticket ID.

SLAs and thresholds
- Standard requests: 24 business hours.
- High-priority (production incident): 4 hours (phone + portal).
- Emergency after-hours: on-call approver phone escalation; retrospective approval within 24 hours.

Approval matrix (examples)
| Resource category | Typical approver(s) | Security review required | Auto-grant allowed? | Max duration |
|-------------------|---------------------|-------------------------:|--------------------:|------------:|
| Non-prod read-only| Team lead            | No                      | Yes                 | 90 days     |
| Non-prod write    | Team lead + SRE      | No                      | Conditional         | 30 days     |
| Prod read         | Product manager + SRE| Conditional              | No                  | 30 days     |
| Prod write        | Product manager + SRE + Security | Yes         | No                  | 7 days      |
| Audit logs access | Security + Compliance| Yes                     | No                  | 7 days      |

RBAC templates (recommended labels)
- role:data-scientist: read-only datasets + dev compute
- role:inference-operator: production inference write, model deploy APIs
- role:observability-reader: metrics/logs read-only (no PII)

CLI example (request automation)
```
# Request temporary role for debugging
rlctl access-request --user alice --role inference-operator --resource project:redwood-prod --duration 6h --reason "investigating latency spike"
```

Change Management
-----------------
Scope: configuration changes to infra, runtime, CI/CD pipelines, production model rollouts, and security controls.

Change categories
- Standard (low-risk, pre-authorized routine changes)
- Normal (planned changes requiring approval and scheduling)
- Emergency (out-of-band fixes for incidents)

Normal change process (numbered)
1. Create RFC in Change Registry (ticket template: ChangeRequest). Include scope, rollback plan, test plan, schedule, owners.
2. Technical review by SRE/Platform and dependency owners.
3. Security and compliance review if change touches data control plane or auth.
4. Scheduled maintenance window and stakeholder notification.
5. Execute change and mark lifecycle states: planned -> staging -> validation -> production -> closed.

Emergency change flow
- On-call SRE follows emergency authorizer list (Primary SRE on-call, then Engineering Manager, then CTO).
- Execute emergency fix and attach retrospective within 48 hours.
- Post-incident RFC must be submitted within 5 business days.

Change guardrails
- All production changes must have automated rollback steps and observability runbooks attached.
- No schema-changing data migrations in production without dry-run and 2 approvers.

Data Management
---------------
Data classification
- Restricted (PII, PHI, financial records): encryption at rest and in transit, access by exception only.
- Internal (product telemetry, internal notes): restricted to employees, aggregated exports require approval.
- Public (marketing materials): permitted for external distribution.

Retention and deletion
- Default retention: product telemetry 90 days (hot), 365 days (cold); logs 180 days.
- Restricted data retention must be approved by Data Governance and Legal.
- Data deletion requests follow standard ticketed workflow and are recorded in the Data Deletion Log.

Data use approvals
- Any project that trains models on customer data must complete a Data Use Assessment and obtain Legal + Security signoff.
- Example: dataset_redwood_customers_2025 requires DU-approved contract & KMS policy.

Encryption and key management
- All production encryption keys must be provisioned via KMS/HSM. Key rotation every 90 days for high-sensitivity keys.

Procurement & Expenses
----------------------
Procurement thresholds and approvals
| Amount band (USD) | Required approvals | Procurement channel |
|-------------------:|--------------------|-------------------|
| <$2,500            | Manager            | Card/ExpensesApp  |
| $2,500–$25,000     | Manager + Finance  | ProcureFlow (PO)  |
| $25,000–$250,000   | Manager + Finance + Procurement | ProcureFlow + Contracting |
| >$250,000          | Exec sponsor + Legal + Procurement | Strategic sourcing |

Preferred procurement flow
1. Create Purchase Request with justification, budget code, and vendor information.
2. Finance validates budget and is assigned approver.
3. Procurement reviews for preferred vendors and negotiates T&C if applicable.
4. PO is issued; vendor onboarding checklist triggered for new vendors.

Expense policy
- Employees should expense costs within 60 days. Card disputes must be filed within 90 days.
- Travel bookings: Economy or lowest reasonable fare; upgrade only with exec approval.

Vendor Management
-----------------
Vendor risk levels and onboarding checklist
- Risk levels: Low, Medium, High (based on data access, control plane integration, criticality).
- Onboarding steps for new vendor (checklist):
  1. Business justification and owner assignment.
  2. Security questionnaire (VendorRisk) completion.
  3. Contract with minimum security clauses (encryption, breach notification, subprocessor list).
  4. Procurement creates PO and payment terms.
  5. Technical integration review and test plan.
  6. Compliance records stored in Vendor Registry.

Contractual minimums (summary)
- Data processing agreement for any vendor handling customer data.
- Right to audit clause for high-risk vendors.
- Minimum 30-day termination notice and documented exit plan for critical services.

Vendor monitoring
- Quarterly review for medium/high vendors; monthly health checks for critical platform vendors.
- Maintain scorecard: uptime, incident response time, patch cadence, security findings.

Travel Policies
---------------
Pre-approval and booking
- All travel reimbursed must be pre-approved by the Requester’s manager in the TravelPortal.
- Book through TravelPortal or approved agency for company liability coverage.

Per diems and allowable expenses
- Domestic: meals up to $75/day; Lodging: reasonable single occupancy rate.
- International: per-region rates available in TravelPortal templates.
- Alcohol may be expensed only while entertaining clients with prior manager approval.

Safety and emergency
- Employees traveling to countries with Level 3 or higher travel advisories require Security team approval.
- Emergency contact: travel-support@redwood.com and on-call security phone.

Templates & quick artifacts
--------------------------
Included templates (stored in Templates folder in ProcureFlow)\- Access Request form (JSON/YAML example below)
- Purchase Request form
- Change Request (RFC) template
- Vendor Onboarding checklist
- Data Use Assessment template

Access Request JSON example
```
{
  "requester": "alice@redwood.com",
  "role": "inference-operator",
  "resource": "project:redwood-prod",
  "duration_hours": 6,
  "justification": "Investigating model latency spike",
  "approvals_required": ["product_manager", "sre"]
}
```

Purchase Request example fields
- requester_email, vendor_name, item_description, estimated_cost, budget_code, justification, required_by_date, attachments

Escalation and exceptions
-------------------------
- Escalation path for stalled requests: Requester -> Approver -> Owner team lead -> Function head -> People Ops / Finance escalation.
- Exceptions to policy must be documented with risk assessment and approved by the responsible function head and Risk Committee.

Auditability and retention
-------------------------
- All approvals and artifacts are recorded in ProcureFlow and retained for a minimum of 7 years for procurement; access logs retained per Data Retention schedule.
- Regular audits: Quarterly spot-checks for access grants and annual vendor compliance review.

Adoption and tooling notes
------------------------
- Automate low-risk grants via IAM Service and ProcureFlow integrations.
- Integrate VendorRisk and Contracting with ProcureFlow to enforce policy gates before POs are issued.
- Use AuditExports to feed SIEM for all privileged access events.
